What did we include, and where did it come from?
    10 claims stand behind this building, and every one of
      them is in exactly one row here. The tables further down carry them one at a time, with
      the reasoning behind why; the decisions that belong to no single claim are under
      “Liberties taken here”.

    Where did it stand?
    
      
    recorded position
    North-west corner of the court-house square (the public square bounded by Randolph, Clark, Washington and LaSalle), at the Randolph and LaSalle end; fronting north onto Randolph.reconstructed
    sources: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the…; OpenStreetMap contributors. Street centerline…PLACED 2026-08-11. THE CORNER IS DOCUMENTED AND THE COORDINATE IS DERIVED, so the tag follows the weaker half. Andreas puts the log jail on 'the northwest corner of the court-house square'. The public square is the block bounded by Randolph Street on the north, Washington Street on the south, Clark Street on the east and LaSalle Street on the west - the block this project's own ground control identifies as such in the wright 1834 gcps data, where LaSalle and Randolph is labelled 'NW corner of the Public Square block' and Clark and Washington 'SE corner of the Public Square block'. Its four inside corners were computed for this parcel from modern OpenStreetMap intersection centres fetched 2026-08-11, offset 12.2 m into the block on each axis, half of an 80 ft street per Hathaway 1834: NW 447538.25 / 4637130.78, NE 447639.27 / 4637130.25, SW 447541.20 / 4637018.49, SE 447639.80 / 4637018.05, which makes the block about 101 x 112 m. The jail's own north-west corner is set on the square's north-west corner, so the footprint origin - which is the building's south-west corner - sits its own depth south of it. THIS IS A CORNER OF A BLOCK, NOT A LOT, so it is a weaker statement than the corner-lot placements elsewhere in this dataset: nothing says how far into the block the building stood, whether it was set back from either street line, or which way it faced. WORKING UNCERTAINTY ABOUT 20 M from the georeference (the datum data: 17.5 m RMS on Wright 1834, 3.7 per cent paper stretch), plus an unquantified setback into the block. Facade bearing 0, due north onto Randolph, CONVENTION RATHER THAN EVIDENCE - a jail at the north-west corner could as reasonably have faced west onto LaSalle or inward onto the square, and nothing attests it. The square itself in 1835 was otherwise an open, unimproved prairie block, fenced or not; no fence, path or improvement of the block is modelled. RECONCILED WITH THE COMMITTED PLAT 2026-08-28, AND THE CLAIM DID NOT MOVE - ONLY THE LINE IT WAS DERIVED AGAINST. The method above found the square's north-west corner by taking modern OpenStreetMap intersection centres, fetched 2026-08-11, and stepping 12.2 m into the block on each axis. That is not this project's own Randolph Street: the committed centreline in the 1835 streets data, offset by half the committed 80 ft corridor, is what the plat lots generator builds every platted block edge from, and it is the line every derived layer in this scene reads. Measured against it with the corridor intrusion check, this footprint's north wall stood 3.48 m OUT PAST block 39's Randolph frontage line, in the platted roadway, with its centroid inside the corridor - deeper than any of the four Lake Street records other work looked at - and the frontage works generator refused two steps of Randolph's plank walk, 0.0 to 10.4 m along that face, naming this building in the refusal. THE REPAIR IS THIS RECORD'S OWN METHOD RUN AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S OWN LINE: the footprint is translated 4.981 m along the face's inward normal - dE -0.040 m, dN -4.981 m in local ENU, so UTM E 447538.25 N 4637126.21 becomes E 447538.21 N 4637121.23 - which leaves its north wall 1.50 m back from the committed frontage line. THE SQUARE IS NOT SUBDIVIDED, so there is no lot line to stand off: 1.50 m is plat occupancy lot margin m, the plat module's own margin off a boundary, and it is the same figure the reconciled South Water and Lake records took off their lot lines. NOTHING ALONG THE STREET MOVED: the along-face position, the block, the corner and the side are untouched, and so is the confidence grade - re-deriving a coordinate from better geometry is not new evidence, and Andreas's 'northwest corner of the court-house square' is what it always was. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REPAIR: the 20 m working uncertainty stated above is unchanged and dwarfs this 4.98 m, so the move is a reconciliation between two of this project's own lines and not a claim to have located the jail better. The facade bearing stays 0 while this face runs at 0.46 degrees, which leaves the front wall between 1.50 and 1.55 m back across its width; that skew is not corrected here, because rotating a record is a second claim and this one is a repair. V4 ENCLOSURE/ACCESS RECONSTRUCTION 2026-10-30: the earlier exact northing was a chosen setback derived from the public-square street line, not an attested building coordinate. Andreas attests the northwest part of the square, not the exact setback. Move only 1.30 m south within the stated roughly20 m working uncertainty, retaining easting, bearing, core fabric, footprint, parcel and every committed street input. This finite R placement allows the existing1.80 m native doorway approach plus0.25 m to the continuous palisade axis atN-269.25 (0.16 m beyond a180 mm backing post), rather than preserving an invented centre gap that is absent from the1902 drawing. The exact1.30 m is an access/layout convention, not survey evidence or a measured pictorial distance. The1836-captioned plate does not establish the July1835 arrangement; continuity remains R. The earlier placement and plat-reconciliation history above is retained as history, not a claim that the later R setback is derived.
    why
  
    
  
      
    Was it inside the town's fire limit?
    Inside the limit — hay could not lawfully be stacked here.
    Section 22 of the by-laws the Trustees passed on
      5 August 1835 made it unlawful to stack hay inside a boundary they walked street
      by street — 198.9 acres
      of it — under twenty-five dollars a stack. It is the town's own statement of where
      it was built up closely enough to burn, five weeks after this scene.
    commencing on Washington street, at the United States Reservation, and running thence West to the intersection of Canal Street, thence North to the intersection of Kinzie Street, thence East to the intersection of Wolcott street, thence to Illinois Street, and thence to Lake Michigan
    The Chicago Democrat, 19 August 1835, page 1 —
      the limit is derived from committed street lines, never drawn in the scene.
  
      
    Was it here?
    
      
    recorded standing
    1833-10-01 → 1835-12-31inferred
    sources: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the…Andreas: 'During the fall of 1833, the citizens felt that something more metropolitan was required than the estray pen', and a log jail was built (the research notes on structures south section 7, from Andreas I scan pp. 367 and 1243). A SEASON IS THE WHOLE OF THE DATING. 1833-10-01 is the middle of a northern-Illinois autumn and is a bound rather than a date; the building is standing well before the scene date on any reading of 'fall'. THE END IS A HOUSEKEEPING BOUND, NOT A DEMOLITION DATE - nothing reached says when this jail came down or was replaced, and 1835-12-31 is the ordinary continuity cut at the scene year this dataset uses where a fate is unattested.
    why
  
    
  
      
    Was it this shape?
    
      
    footprint
    reconstructed
    INVENTED. NO SOURCE REACHED GIVES THIS BUILDING A DIMENSION, a plan, or a number of cells. 6.096 x 4.572 m is 20 x 15 ft, recorded converted with the original figures stated per the datum json's data units rule. The only constraint the evidence offers is relative and it runs in both directions: the jail was built because something more metropolitan was required than the estray pen, so it is a more substantial thing than a stock pound; and it was itself superseded within a few years, so it was small. A 20 x 15 ft log box is a two-cell lock-up and is the smallest thing that answers both. Nothing else about the shape is a finding: the plain rectangle, the proportion and the scale are all this record's.

        Attributes and evidence
        
    built
    1833attested
    sources: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the…Andreas: the log jail was built in the fall of 1833.
    why
  
    construction
    logattested
    sources: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the…The building is named a LOG jail in the only description this project has of it, which makes the material the single best-attested thing about it. THE PLATE NOW SETTLES THE SECOND HALF OF IT: the engraving of the first Cook County jail in the owner's 2026-08-18 brief (the source files for owner brief of 2026-08-18, image 1) draws squared timber laid horizontally — 'a low log jail — squared timber, near-flat roof' — which is hewn log in courses with notched corners, exactly what this archetype builds for this value (the logwork generator). Until 2026-08-21 this note said hewn-versus-round was unattested and the archetype's hewn wall was a convention standing where evidence should be; the plate is that evidence, at a modern reconstruction, for the FABRIC and not for any dimension. Whether the walls were single or doubled, and whether they were lined inside, nothing reached says. The plate is a PICTORIAL (a modern reconstruction) held here as the brief's written record rather than a committed binary — the images were supplied in-session and other work owns identifying them against the Andreas plate numbering and creating the source record — so it is cited by path, the way this dataset's other brief-driven attributes are (Green Tree Tavern chimneys, image 6). The value's own grade is unchanged: 'log' was attested by Andreas before the plate and still is.
    why
  
    function
    jailattested
    sources: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the…Purpose-built for confinement, and it is the building that ended the practice recorded on the Estray pen record - prisoners held in the stock pound for want of anywhere else. Cook County was organised in 1831 and the county's business was conducted in rented rooms; this is the first purpose-built county structure of any kind and it precedes the court-house on the same block by about two years.
    why
  
    door
    maninferred
    Not attested. `door` in this archetype names what has to get through the opening rather than whether there was one. A jail takes a person through in hand and nothing else - no horse, no wagon - so the man-door class is the reading, and it is the only one whose 1.88 m clear height fits under this wall. Where the door stood, what it was made of, and whether it was barred or grated is not attested and is the archetype's default.
    why
  
    roof pitch deg
    12inferred
    12 DEGREES, THE PLATE'S NEAR-FLAT ROOF INSTEAD OF THIS ARCHETYPE'S DEFAULT. Superseded 2026-08-21. The value was 32.0 — the outbuilding archetype's own gable default, kept deliberately on 2026-08-11 because nothing attested a pitch and a fresh guess would have looked like a finding. The engraving of the first cook county jail in the owner's 2026-08-18 brief (the source files for owner brief of 2026-08-18, image 1) is that evidence, and it is about this particular building: 'a low log jail — squared timber, near-flat roof'. A convention loses to a picture of the thing itself, so the pitch comes down. 12 degrees is the reading of 'near-flat' at this building's scale — 0.49 m of rise over the 2.29 m half-span, a cap on a box rather than a cabin's gable, and the whole building 0.94 m lower to its ridge than it stood yesterday. NOT LOWER THAN THAT, and the floor is the covering: this archetype roofs an outbuilding in boards laid down the slope rather than shingles (the outbuilding generator _roof plane), and a lapped board roof weighted or nailed down is the frontier form that goes near-flat where a riven-shake field cannot — the archetype's own note puts shakes at about 18 degrees minimum. WHAT IS INFERRED IS THAT THE PITCH IS LOW, NOT THAT IT IS 12: no plate can be measured to a degree, and a pictorial (a modern reconstruction) may drive form and never a dimension of the ground.
    why
  
    roof type
    gableinferred
    GABLE IS KEPT, AND THE PLATE IS WHY THE PITCH MOVED RATHER THAN THE FORM. The engraving of the first cook county jail in the owner's 2026-08-18 brief (the source files for owner brief of 2026-08-18, image 1) draws a near-flat roof. That is a statement about PITCH — this record's roof pitch (deg) now carries it — and it is not a statement about whether the roof fell one way or two: the brief holds the plate as a written description, and 'near-flat' distinguishes neither. So the form stays what it was reasoned to on 2026-08-11, and the reasoning is unchanged: gable is the near-universal roof form for log construction of this type, period and region, and it is what this project's other log buildings carry. The archetype would default a building this shallow to a shed roof, which is a covering appropriate to a lean-to; a purpose-built county jail is stated as gabled rather than left to that default. Typological derivation, not a measurement — and a single-slope reading of the same plate would be a legitimate rival that nothing this project holds can settle.
    why
  
    wall height (m)
    2.66inferred
    No figure is attested. 2.66 m is about 8 ft 9 in to the plate: a man's standing height with a header over the door and a course or two above it, which is what a lock-up needs and no more. It is also, to the centimetre, what this archetype's own size-aware default computes for a 20 x 15 ft footprint, and it is kept deliberately. THE PLATE CORROBORATES THE DIRECTION AND DOES NOT REPLACE THE NUMBER: the engraving of the first Cook County jail in the owner's 2026-08-18 brief (the source files for owner brief of 2026-08-18, image 1) draws a low, squat building, which is what a 2.66 m wall under a near-flat roof already is, and moving the figure to match a picture that carries no scale would be inventing a measurement out of an impression. What is inferred is that the height falls in this range, not that it is exactly 2.66 m. The squatness the plate shows is carried by roof pitch (deg), which is the attribute the plate can actually speak to.
